fixes.explanation: True. Paul says the Father "…has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light." (Colossians 1:12). Notice who does the qualifying: the Father. The Colossians are the ones who get to share, and the Father is the one who qualified them.

Church makes sense as a guess, since Paul is writing to a group of believers at Colossae (Colossians 1:2). But the verse says Epaphras "…also informed us of your love in the Spirit." (Colossians 1:8). The blank asks what their love is in, and Paul answers with the Spirit, not a group of people. The believers are who Paul writes to, and the Spirit is what he says their love is in.

Paul doesn't put it that way. He prays for knowledge "…so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord and may please Him in every way…" (Colossians 1:10). The knowledge leads to a walk that pleases the Lord, so it's about how they live once they know His will. Earning isn't in the picture, because Paul says it's the Father who "…has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light." (Colossians 1:12). The Father does the qualifying, and the walk follows.

Record sounds close, but Paul doesn't say it. He writes, "…in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins." (Colossians 1:14). A record of sins would only keep them on file. Forgiveness is a different thing, because it means the sins are forgiven, and Paul says that's what we have in the Son.
